references.text: The expression "in the beginning" (ἐν ἀρχῇ) in Gen 1:1 forms the background for John's prologue. By linking the Word to "the beginning," John shows that the Word already existed when all things were created.

The wisdom in Prov 8:22-31 speaks of having been with God from the beginning, before creation. This reflects John's statement that the Word was "in the beginning with God," and points to the eternal existence of the Word together with the Father.

John 1:1 says that "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." Verse 2 summarizes and confirms this by repeating that "He was in the beginning with God," emphasizing the Word's eternal fellowship with the Father.

In John 17:5 Jesus prays: "Glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the world began." This shows that the Son shared glory with the Father before creation, which corresponds to the Word being with God "in the beginning."
In John 17:24 Jesus speaks of the Father loving him "before the foundation of the world was laid." This confirms the eternal fellowship between the Father and the Son that John 1:2 points to.

Phil 2:6 says that Christ "was in the form of God" and did not consider equality with God something to be grasped. This confirms the Word's eternal divine existence with the Father, in agreement with John 1:2.
Col 1:17 says that Christ "is before all things, and in him all things hold together." This emphasizes Christ's pre-existence and his eternal being with God, consistent with John 1:2.
Heb 1:2 says that God "has spoken to us through the Son … by whom he made the world." This confirms the Son's existence with the Father before creation, in agreement with John 1:2.

1 John 1:1-2 speaks of "the word of life" which "was with the Father and was revealed to us." John uses the same language as in the prologue of the Gospel to describe the Word's eternal existence with the Father.
